correctness.rationale: For any index set I of cardinality at least two, product membership fibers are boxes. If Separation holds for finite counting test F, the two-coordinate relation F(ab)=1 is rectangular and symmetric, hence F is zero or multiplicative. A nonzero multiplicative eventually constant Boolean function on nonnegative integers must equal 1, 1_{n>=1}, or 1_{n=1}. Each admits an internal coordinatewise separator (using external choice and Replacement). For every other test the nonrectangle furnishes two accepted opposite corners and rejected cross-corner in a four-element product fiber. A <=3-element nonempty box varies in at most one coordinate, so no formula can give a smaller witness. checker.py verified 1016 truncated truth tables (988 counterexample tables), 1728 triple-product configurations, and explicit witnesses; finite checks only corroborate the general proof.

value.rationale: The motivating set-theoretic direct-power construction identifies positive Horn as a sufficient scheme class without an exact reverse boundary. Membership-fiber size predicates form a canonical and complete Boolean threshold fragment used throughout finite model theory. The theorem classifies its entire spectrum, gives a non-positive-Horn syntactic survivor (exact singleton), and proves a sharp universal four-member witness for every failure, rather than one unmotivated parameter instance.
